accidents: isoformat_utc replaces every '+00:00' of isoformat(), so an offset of +00:00:30 is written 'Z:30' and +00:00:00.000001 'Z:00.000001' (time_utils.py:70)

store_rows._dt and v8._as_dt replace every 'Z' before parsing, so a Z anywhere becomes '+00:00' there: 'Z' as the date/time separator or a second Z is spliced into the text (store_rows.py:71, v8.py:145); parse_event_ts replaces only a trailing Z (time_utils.py:45)
fromisoformat takes any one character, non-ASCII included, as the date/time separator, and every reader above inherits it

fromisoformat (CPython's C parser) reads an offset of zero hours, minutes and seconds with a fraction, +00:00:00.5, as UTC, the fraction dropped, while +02:00:00.5 keeps it; reads offset minutes or seconds of 60 as carrying (+12:60 is +13:00); reads what follows a fourth ':' of the time as its fraction (08:09:10:5 is 08:09:10.5); takes a fraction after the hour or the minute (08,5 is 08:00:00.5); and takes '.' or ',' between an offset's hours and minutes (+02.00). Every reader above inherits these (time_utils.py:46, store_rows.py:71, v8.py:145, origin_history.py:398)

pydantic's JSON spelling (responses) rounds an offset's total_seconds() half away from zero to whole seconds, then writes Z for zero and else whole minutes: +00:00:00.5 is '+00:00', +00:00:00.499999 'Z', +00:00:59.999999 '+00:01'

formatters.str: str(dt): what default=str spells in log payloads

marks: platform_dependent: {other: the result on Linux and macOS, win32: on Windows where known; a platform not named is not known}, for fromtimestamp (and ulid_time) outside 1970..3000, which Windows' gmtime_s refuses; platform_dependent: true and local_time_dependent: true as datetime.jsonl (strftime %Y below 1000, a naive value through astimezone). Every unmarked fromtimestamp and strftime cell equals its pure-Python spelling
records: datetime: fields and offset_us (the offset in microseconds) through each formatter; text (or text_cps when it holds a surrogate) through each parser; timestamp (IEEE-754 bits and repr) through datetime.fromtimestamp(x, tz=timezone.utc), as isoformat(). Each result is v, or error: the exception type
